entries.name: Consensus decision-making
entries.definition: A group decision process that seeks the agreement of all participants rather than a majority vote.

entries.name: Constant Contact
entries.definition: An online email marketing service for building and sending email campaigns and managing contact lists.

entries.name: Constituent relationship management
entries.definition: Managing the relationships of a nonprofit or public body with its donors, members and other constituents, usually with CRM software.

entries.name: ConstraintLayout
entries.definition: An Android layout manager that positions and sizes views using constraints relative to other views and to the parent.

entries.name: Construct (game engine)
entries.definition: A 2D game engine from Scirra that uses a visual editor and event sheets so that games can be made with little or no coding.

entries.name: Constructing dental study casts
entries.definition: Pouring and trimming dental impressions in gypsum to make study casts, the models of a patient's teeth used for diagnosis and treatment planning.

entries.name: Construction management software
entries.definition: Software for planning, tracking and coordinating construction projects, including schedules, budgets and documents.

entries.name: Consumer engagement
entries.definition: Building and sustaining interaction between a brand and its consumers across channels.

entries.name: Contact management software
entries.definition: Software for storing and organising contact details and the history of interactions with each contact.

entries.name: Contact tracing
entries.definition: A public health method of identifying and notifying people who were exposed to someone with an infectious disease, so that spread can be limited.

entries.name: Content curation
entries.definition: Selecting, organising and presenting existing material from many sources for a chosen audience.

entries.name: Contingency planning
entries.definition: Preparing plans for responding to events that could disrupt normal operations.

entries.name: Continued process verification
entries.definition: Ongoing collection and analysis of manufacturing data to confirm that a validated process stays in a state of control, a stage of process validation in regulated industries.

entries.name: Continuous passive motion
entries.definition: A rehabilitation therapy in which a machine moves a joint through a set range of motion without effort from the patient, often after joint surgery.

entries.name: Contour plowing
entries.definition: Plowing across a slope along its elevation contours rather than up and down it, to slow water runoff and soil erosion.

entries.name: Contract review
entries.definition: Reading a contract to check its terms, obligations and risks against what a party needs or the law allows.

entries.name: Control loops
entries.definition: Feedback arrangements in which a controller compares a measured value with a setpoint and adjusts an output to keep them close, as in process and automation engineering.

entries.name: Control valves and flow characteristics
entries.definition: How valves that regulate fluid flow in process plants work, and how the flow through them changes with valve opening (for example linear, equal-percentage and quick-opening).

entries.name: ControlLogix
entries.definition: A family of programmable automation controllers from Rockwell Automation (Allen-Bradley) that run industrial machines and processes.

entries.name: ControlUp
entries.definition: Software for monitoring and troubleshooting virtual desktops, servers and end-user devices in IT environments.

entries.name: Conversational AI
entries.definition: Building software, such as chatbots and voice assistants, that talks with people in everyday language.

entries.name: Convolutional neural networks
entries.definition: A type of neural network that applies learned filters across grid-like data such as images, widely used in computer vision.

entries.name: Copier troubleshooting
entries.definition: Diagnosing and fixing faults in photocopiers and multifunction office machines, such as paper jams and print-quality problems.

entries.name: Coping saw
entries.definition: A hand saw with a thin, narrow blade held in a U-shaped frame, used to cut curves in wood and to trim moulding joints.

entries.name: Coppermine Photo Gallery
entries.definition: A free, open-source web application, written in PHP, for hosting and managing online photo galleries.

entries.name: Copywriting
entries.definition: Writing text for advertising, marketing and other persuasive material.

entries.name: Core Spotlight
entries.definition: An Apple framework for adding an app's content to the on-device Spotlight search index.

entries.name: CoreOS
entries.definition: A minimal Linux-based operating system built for running applications in containers on clusters of servers.

entries.name: Corona SDK
entries.definition: A cross-platform software development kit for building 2D mobile apps and games with the Lua scripting language.

entries.name: Coronal polishing
entries.definition: Polishing the crown surfaces of teeth to remove plaque and stain, a task often done by dental assistants and hygienists.

entries.name: Corporate communications
entries.definition: Managing an organisation's messages to employees, investors, the media and the public.

entries.name: Corporate finance
entries.definition: The field concerned with how companies raise money, invest it and manage their capital to create value for their owners.

entries.name: Correspondent banking
entries.definition: Arrangements in which one bank provides services such as payments and account access to another bank, often across borders.

entries.name: Cosmetic dermatology
entries.definition: The branch of dermatology that improves the appearance of skin, hair and nails, for example with fillers, lasers and peels.

entries.name: COSO framework
entries.definition: A framework published by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission for designing and assessing internal control and enterprise risk management.

entries.name: Cost accounting
entries.definition: The part of accounting that records and analyses the costs of making goods or providing services so managers can control and price them.

entries.name: Cost estimating
entries.definition: Predicting what a project, product or job will cost before it is done.

entries.name: Cost to serve
entries.definition: A way of working out how much it costs a business to serve each customer, product or channel, counting activities such as delivery, handling and support.

entries.name: CoStar Real Estate Manager
entries.definition: A CoStar Group cloud software product for managing leases, property portfolios and real-estate costs.

entries.name: Counterparty risk
entries.definition: The risk that the other party to a financial contract will fail to meet its obligations.
